newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus rises again in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus rises again in July.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus recorded another hefty jump in data released on Monday, growing 69.7 percent in July from a year earlier, but economists said the rise was at the lower end of their forecasts.
The overall surplus came in at 849.08 billion yen, while the surplus with the United States grew 35.7 percent to 420.55 billion yen, the Ministry of Finance said.
Economists' forecasts had ranged from a 60 percent to a 114 percent increase in the overall surplus.
At the exchange rate of around 118 yen to the dollar early on Monday, the overall customs-cleared trade surplus was $7.19 billion, while the surplus with the United States was $3.56 billion.
July's sharp rise follows dramatic increases in April and May and is expected to add further kindling to trade tensions with Washington over the expanding surplus.

"Although the overall trend continues to favour a widening of Japan's surplus, clearly this number is below consensus," said Jane Berryman, fixed income analyst at Technical Data. "But I think the thing that is pertinent right now is that the surplus with the U.S. is at 420.5 billion yen."

U.S. officials said they are concerned that Japan's surplus could keep rising into next year, particularly if car exports to the United States continue to increase while car imports continue to slow on weak demand in Japan.
Japanese officials say, however, that the pace of increase in the surplus will slow and that structural reforms in the economy will work to bring it down.

A Finance Ministry official told reporters after the release of the data that there was a continuation of structural changes in Japan since 1993, such as manufacturers expanding production overseas, increased imports of finished products and financial market deregulation.
"I don't think the trade surplus will continue to expand drastically as a trend," he said.

The dollar edged up against the yen after the trade surplus came out at the lower end of market expectations, but traders said the focus was now on the Japanese stock market, which fell in the wake of Friday's sharp drop on Wall Street.
In mid-morning trading, the dollar was at 117.70 yen after ending in New York at 117.40 on Friday, and the Nikkei stock average was down some 369 points or about two percent at 18,957.
